Time-varying impulse responses, variance decompositions and forecasts of a TVP-VAR

Source: R/tvp.R
tvp_dynamics.Rd

Impulse responses are computed at a date by freezing the parameters at their date-t values (the standard "local" IRF of Cogley-Sargent / Primiceri): $$\Theta_h(t)=\Phi_h(B_t)\,A_t^{-1}\Lambda_t^{1/2},\qquad \Phi_h=\sum_{l=1}^{\min(h,p)}A_l(t)\Phi_{h-l},$$ i.e. the response of \(y_{t+h}\) to a one-standard-deviation recursive shock if the economy were to stay at the date-\(t\) parameters. Note that the shock size \(\Lambda_t^{1/2}\) varies with the date, so changes in the IRF mix changes in propagation and in volatility; use normalise = list(shock =, variable =, size =) to hold the impact response fixed (e.g. a 25bp rate shock) and isolate changes in propagation. The FEVD uses the same frozen-parameter responses. The identification is recursive in the order of the data.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'tvpvar'
irf(
  object,
  date = NULL,
  horizon = 20L,
  level = c(0.68, 0.9),
  normalise = NULL,
  cumulative = NULL,
  ...,
  .fevd = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'tvpvar'
fevd(object, date = NULL, horizon = 20L, level = c(0.68, 0.9), ...)

# S3 method for class 'tvpvar'
forecast(object, h = 8L, level = c(0.68, 0.9), drift = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

object

a tvpvar() fit.

date

one or several dates (matched to the nearest element of object$dates: the ts time stamp if Y was a ts, else the row index of Y), or "last"/"first". Default: the last date.

horizon

maximum horizon (impact is horizon 0).

level

credible/confidence levels (e.g. c(0.68, 0.90)); bands are equal-tailed percentiles.

normalise

optional normalise_to() specification (the older list(shock =, variable =, size =) still works): rescale each shock so that the impact response of variable equals size (e.g. a 100bp policy-rate shock).

cumulative

<tidy-select> variables whose responses are cumulated over the horizon (use for variables entered in differences), e.g. cumulative = c(infl, unemp).

...

unused.

.fevd

internal; compute the variance decomposition instead of the IRF.

h

forecast horizon (steps).

drift

simulate future parameter drift (TRUE) or freeze parameters at the last date.

Value

for irf/fevd: a varm_irf/varm_fevd (single date, plottable) or a named list of them of class tvpvar_irf (several dates). forecast returns a varm_forecast.

Details

Forecasts simulate, for every stored posterior draw, future paths of \(\beta,\alpha,\log\lambda\) as random walks with the draw's own \(Q,S,W\) (drift = TRUE), so predictive densities include the possibility that parameters keep moving; drift = FALSE freezes them at the end-of-sample values.

Economic intuition. Comparing irf(fit, date = c(1975, 2005)) asks whether, say, the output response to a monetary tightening was larger in the 1970s than in the Great Moderation. Bands reflect posterior uncertainty about the date-specific parameters only; they do not reflect uncertainty about how long the parameters stay put.

See also

Other TVP-VAR: irf_path(), tidy.tvpvar(), tvp_prior(), tvp_volatility(), tvpvar()
